chunks: What Ḥumayd ibn Ziyād narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad al-Kindī, from more than one person, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who dies and has no one present to perform ghusl for him except women: may the women perform ghusl for him? He said: His wife or a woman who is a mahram may perform ghusl for him, and the women should pour water over him, pouring it from above the clothes.

key_terms.النِّسَاءُ: women present in the circumstance described
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: the water used for the ritual washing
key_terms.امْرَأَتُهُ: his wife, who is permitted here to perform ghusl for him
key_terms.ذَاتُ مَحْرَمٍ: a woman within prohibited degrees of marriage to him, allowed here due to kinship
key_terms.مِنْ فَوْقِ الثِّيَابِ: from above the clothes, indicating the manner of washing in this case
key_terms.يُغَسِّلُهُ: to perform the ritual washing of the deceased for him

ai.seo_question: Can women perform ghusl for a deceased man if no men are available?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about ghusl for a deceased man when no male washer is available. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام permits his wife or a mahram woman to wash him, with water being poured over him from above the clothes. It addresses funeral rulings, ritual purity, and family-related legal limits.
